title: Chain of Exemplars Curation Lab
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal lab notes for exploring rotating chains of exemplars (few-shot sequences where exemplars are sampled/rotated across calls) to reduce brittle overfitting to a fixed shotset and to measure stability regressions across versions.

Context / motivation:
- Fixed few-shot sets can cause the model to latch on to spurious surface patterns. Rotating exemplars might improve generalization and reduce single-shot catastrophic drift.
- Want an inexpensive client-side strategy for apps that can't or won't run expensive evals for each model version.
- Investigate operational patterns: rotation frequency, selection heuristics, weighting, caching tradeoffs.

Open hypotheses:
1) Rotating exemplars reduces variance in model outputs measured across prompt restarts for the same user query.
2) Including deliberately adversarial exemplars (edge cases) at low frequency acts as a regression sentinel.
3) Rotation combined with exemplar clustering (semantic diversity) will beat random sampling.

Experiment matrix (rough):
- Variables:
  * rotation_strategy: fixed-sequence | round-robin | weighted-sampling | cluster-sampling
  * exemplar_pool_size: 8 | 16 | 32
  * shots_per_prompt: 2 | 4 | 8
  * adversarial-injection-rate: 0% | 5% | 15%
  * cache_ttl: none | short(5s) | medium(30s)
- Metrics:
  * surface-stability: token-level edit distance across N runs (N=10)
  * semantic-consistency: embedding cosine variance (use redwood embeddings)
  * utility: task-specific accuracy/F1 if labeled dataset available
  * cost: average tokens / request (account for exemplar tokens)
  * latency impact: median p50/p90

Quick sampling heuristics to try:
- diversity-first: pick exemplars by max pairwise embedding distance until shots_per_prompt reached
- recency-bias: prefer exemplars from latest user interactions with decay lambda=0.7
- sentinel-seeding: always include 1 sentinel exemplar from a curated edge-case set when model version changes

Prototype client pseudocode (notes):
- maintain exemplar_pool metadata: {id, embedding, last_used_ts, tags, label(if any), difficulty_score}
- on request: build prompt by sampling according to strategy, assemble in order: seeds -> exemplars -> user_query -> instruction footer
- include meta-token to mark exemplar provenance for downstream evals (e.g., "[EXEMPLAR: id=xx src=curated]")

Observed fragilities so far (small ad-hoc runs):
- Naive random rotation increased surface variance but sometimes reduced semantic accuracy on small high-precision tasks (classification).
- Cluster-sampling + sentinel worked best for regression detection (small n experiments).
- Weighting by difficulty_score seems helpful to maintain performance but can reintroduce bias toward a few exemplars (need exponential backoff).

Representative few-shot templates (samples to test):
- Classification (intent):
  Prompt start: "You are an intent classifier. Use the examples to learn the label patterns. Respond ONLY with the label."
  Example formatting (shot): "EX: Query: "Schedule meeting next week" -> Intent: schedule"
  Shots: sample according to strategy; at end: "Query: "{user_query}" -> Intent:"

- Rewrite (style transfer):
  "Rewrite the sentence to be concise and formal. Examples: 
  Ex1: "Can we meet?" -> "Are you available for a meeting?"
  ...
  Input: "{user_query}"
  Output:"

Failure cases to track (logging keys):
- hallucinated_metadata: model invents entity attributes not present in exemplars or query
- exemplar-binding: model copies irrelevant exemplar-specific tokens into response (we see names/ids leaking)
- label-drift: classification label distribution shifts after exemplar rotation (monitor class-level precision/recall)

Short-term todo (for next week):
- [ ] Build harness GH issue and minimal CSV seed pool (100 exemplars across 4 intents) (link to GH issue in linked_artifacts)
- [ ] Implement cluster-sampling using existing embedding index (PR skeleton in prompt-harness repo)
- [ ] Add sentinel injection toggle and run smoke tests across 3 model variants (gpt-like-small, open-7b, redwood-optimized-13b if available)
- [ ] Write quick README describing sampling strategies and failure metrics for SRE/SDK folks

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep exemplar tokens short — long exemplars blow up token cost. Consider abbreviated annotations + external reference id.
- Think about exposing rotation policy as a routing header so server-side runtime can do smarter caching (if header stable, runtime can cache KV for exemplar prefix).
- If customer wants deterministic outputs, rotation is not appropriate — surface as a tradeoff in docs.

Experiment log (mini):
- 2024-11-12: initial alpha run (pool 24, shots 4, random rotation). Result: +30% token-level variance vs fixed set; accuracy -3pt on small intent set (n=200).
- 2024-11-20: cluster-sampling pilot (k=6 clusters). Result: variance down ~12% vs random; accuracy recovered to within 1pt of fixed baseline.
- 2024-12-03: sentinel injection 5% on model vX. Result: caught 2 regressions where fixed-shot tests missed behavior to do with new tokenization quirk.

Questions / follow-ups:
- How expensive to run per-request clustering in production vs precomputing sharded buckets? (ask infra/infra-data)
- Can console expose per-route exemplar policy knobs for enterprise customers? (product question)
- Should sentinel exemplars be included in unit/smoke evals at deployment time? (ops + QA)

Scratch brain dump end. Keep this as an evolving lab doc.

-- Ava
